subject: Follow-up: $/1M token target + data-residency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olly Green <olly@paytronics.com>, Sana Patel <sana.p@paytronics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap + quick asks (token targets & residency)

Thanks again for the quick demo today — great context on Paytronics' fraud-monitoring workload. Short recap and three quick asks so we can put together a scoped price card.

Recap: you described:
- Production target: ~50M tokens/month initially, with peak bursts up to ~200k tokens/min for reconciliation jobs.
- Primary sensitive traffic: EU customer PII must remain in-region (legal requirement).
- Secondary traffic: anonymized telemetry and models for non-PII ok in US.

What I need from you to finalize options:
1) Budget band for inference (monthly committed spend) — rough range is fine (e.g., $5k–$20k/mo).
2) Target $/1M tokens you expect or consider acceptable at scale. This helps us generate a commit/disc schedule.
3) Confirmation: EU residency requirement applies to all reconciliation logs + training prompts? (we heard just customer PII but want explicit list).

What I’ll share after we get the above:
- Two pricing paths: (A) Full EU residency (all inference in eu-central) with estimated regional premium, (B) Hybrid routing (EU for PII, US for non-PII) with lower blended unit cost.
- Preliminary $/1M token calc and commit tiers (attached redwood-pricing-preview.xlsx).
- SOC2 summary and network diagram (attached soc2-summary.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- If you can send the budget band + residency confirmation by EOD Wed, we’ll have a tuned pricing sheet and SE/ops checklist ready for the technical deep-dive on Friday.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments:
- redwood-pricing-preview.xlsx (preview pricing and commit examples)
- soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope + controls)
From: Olly Green <olly@paytronics.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick asks (token targets & residency)

Appreciate the recap, Marissa. Quick answers below — will pull some more exact numbers after I check with finance.

- Budget band: ballpark monthly spend we can commit to today is roughly $3k–$8k. If discounts are available at commit, we can stretch.
- Target $/1M tokens: we were hoping for something around $1,500 per 1M tokens at scale (this is what we modeled).
- Residency: EU residency requirement applies to customer PII and any raw reconciliation traces that include account identifiers. Aggregated telemetry can leave region.

Also, can you confirm whether EU-hosted inference still supports the same model variants you demoed (low-latency quantized variants)? If not, we need to understand the perf delta.

—Olly
Olly Green
Head of Platform Engineering, Paytronics
olly@paytronics.com | +44 20 7946 0789
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olly Green <olly@paytronics.com>, Sana Patel <sana.p@paytronics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 14:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick asks (token targets & residency)

Thanks — super helpful, Olly. Couple fast clarifications and an initial unit-econ sketch so you can see the tradeoffs.

1) Model parity in EU: we support the same quantized low-latency variants in eu-central-1; performance is functionally identical but there is a regional cost premium (infra and compliance overhead).

2) Unit economics (example):
- Baseline US list: $1,200 per 1M tokens (no commit).
- Typical EU premium: +18% → $1,416 per 1M (this reflects infra + data residency overhead).
- Committed discount: e.g., 25% off at 50M tokens/month → blended to ~$1,062/1M in US, ~$1,252/1M in EU.

Quick worked example for your 50M tokens/mo baseline:
- Pay-as-you-go EU: 50 * $1,416 = $70,800/mo (no commit)
- 50M commit, 25% discount: 50 * $1,252 = $62,600/mo (committed, EU-resident)

Notes on options we discussed:
- Hybrid routing: keep PII inference entirely in eu-central to meet residency, route anonymized workloads to our US cluster. This typically lowers blended $/1M by ~10–12% compared to full EU residency.
- Prefix caching + KV cache for reconciliation jobs can cut token costs for repeated context by ~20% or more depending on your prompt overlap. Our SE can estimate once we see a sample prompt set.

Next steps (I’ll take these if you confirm budget band by EOD Wed):
- Karthik will run a quick perf/cost simulation for the hybrid vs full-EU using your burst profile. (Karthik: can you have a draft by Thu AM?)
- We’ll prepare a formal pricing option sheet (attached redwood-pricing-preview.xlsx) and a short SOW outline for a pilot.
- Send over a small sample of the reconciliation prompts/log schema so our SEs can size caching impact.

If the $1,500/1M target is your modeled number, note that with an entry-level commit we can get you very close in blended scenarios — will run exact math in the SE pass.

Thanks —
Marissa
Attachments:
- redwood-pricing-preview.xlsx

Subject: INTERNAL: Prep for Paytronics cost sims (hybrid vs full-EU) — due Thu AM

Karthik / Rishi — tagging you to prep two quick artifacts for Paytronics:
- Karthik: perf & cost sim comparing hybrid routing vs full EU for 50M tokens/mo, burst profile up to 200k tokens/min. Include: per-1M token calc, expected latency delta, and cache savings assumptions. Deadline: Thu 08:00 PT.
- Rishi: list of compliance controls & SOC2 pages that are relevant for EU residency, and a short note on key encryption/KMS options for customer-managed keys. Deadline: Thu 10:00 PT.

Goal: send a polished one-page summary + updated pricing workbook to Olly by Thu 11:00 his time. Olly is leaning toward a blended approach but wants concrete numbers.

Make the cost calc conservative (assume 15% cache benefit) and include a line for incremental ops cost if we recommend dedicated reserved capacity for reconciliation jobs.

Thanks —
Marissa
